cosy-lesson.title: "The older you get the more you understand why people disappear with art, music, books and quiet living.": Anonymous

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Solitude ≠ noise – the state or situation of being alone, especially by choice.

p.em: Example: Spending time in quiet solitude allows me to regain focus and energy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Retreat ≠ advance – to move away from noise or conflict to a quiet, safe place.

p.em: Example: After a intense work week, she likes to retreat into classical music.

cosy-blockquote.p: Appreciation ≠ neglect – recognition and enjoyment of the good qualities of something.

p.em: Example: My appreciation for acoustic guitar music has grown steadily over the years.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fulfillment ≠ empty – a feeling of satisfaction at having achieved or gained something.

p.em: Example: Creative hobbies offer a deep sense of internal fulfillment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Prioritize ≠ ignore – to treat something as more important than other things.

p.em: Example: As we age, we learn to prioritize peace of mind over social popularity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Contemplation ≠ rush – deep, reflective thought or observation.

p.em: Example: Reading philosophy requires calm contemplation and uninterrupted time.

cosy-blockquote.p: Boundary ≠ exposure – a limit that defines acceptable behavior or emotional space.

p.em: Example: Setting firm boundaries helps prevent burnout in busy environments.

cosy-blockquote.p: Unwind ≠ stress – to relax after a period of work or tension.

p.em: Example: I usually unwind by listening to ambient records in the evening.

cosy-blockquote.p: Refuge ≠ danger – a condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit or trouble.

p.em: Example: Books were her main refuge during stressful childhood years.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nurture ≠ destroy – to care for and encourage the growth or development of something.

p.em: Example: Quiet evenings help nurture our creative imagination.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why is solitude often seen as a sign of emotional maturity rather than loneliness?
★ When do you feel the strongest need for personal solitude?

How does artistic expression act as a safe refuge from daily work pressure?
★ What place or activity serves as your personal refuge?

Why do we learn to prioritize personal peace over societal expectations as we grow older?
★ What is one priority that has become much clearer to you recently?

How does spending time in deep contemplation improve our decision-making skills?
★ Do you set aside dedicated time for quiet contemplation?

Why are clear personal boundaries essential for maintaining quiet living?
★ Have you ever had to set a firm boundary to protect your rest time?

How does literature help us nurture our inner life and emotional depth?
★ Which book helped nurture your curiosity the most?

Why is finding effective ways to unwind crucial in modern high-speed careers?
★ What is your favorite ritual to unwind after a tense day?

How does developing an appreciation for simple arts change our daily outlook?
★ What simple form of art do you appreciate most?

Why can a quiet, peaceful home provide a deeper sense of fulfillment than social status?
★ What gives you the deepest feeling of personal fulfillment?

Why do some artists choose to retreat from public life to focus entirely on their craft?
★ Would you enjoy spending a week on a remote retreat without internet?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our lifestyle choices and art appreciation.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our lifestyle choices and art appreciation.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Modern social media makes genuine solitude nearly impossible for young adults. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Can someone experience true solitude while keeping a smartphone nearby?

A society that values constant busywork will eventually lose its appreciation for fine literature. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think people read fewer books today than thirty years ago?

The true purpose of art is to offer a peaceful refuge from real-world chaos. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should art challenge our thoughts or comfort our emotions?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation with teacher in 1-on-1 format.

ul.li: Incorrect: I would rather to stay at home. → Correct: I would rather stay at home. (('Would rather' is followed by a bare infinitive without 'to'.))
Incorrect: I prefer read than watch TV. → Correct: I prefer reading to watching TV. ((Use 'prefer + -ing + to + -ing' when comparing two activities.))
Incorrect: I am used to live in a small town. → Correct: I used to live in a small town. ((Past states use 'used to + verb', not 'am used to + verb'.))
